newsitem.title: USA: CB to acquire Koll Real Estate.
newsitem.headline: CB to acquire Koll Real Estate.

text.p: CB Commercial Real Estate Services Group Inc. said Tuesday it agreed to acquire Koll Real Estate Services in a stock deal valued at more than $165.9 million, including the assumption of debt.

The combined company, to be called CB Commercial, aims to be a global leader in real estate services, offering commercial real estate leasing and sales, property and facilities management, mortgage banking and investment advisory/asset management services.

Under the definitive agreement, which is expected to be signed this week, CB will offer about 5.6 million shares of its common stock for all of Koll in a tax-free purchase. The Los Angeles-based company will also provide warrants to buy an additional 600,000 CB shares at $30 per share. CB will also assume about $35 million of Koll's debt.

CB Chairman and Chief Executive James Didion said he expects immediate savings of $12 million from the merger. It will boost 1997 earnings, excluding a one-time merger charge of an estimated $15 million to $18 million, he said.
The deal, which has been approved by both companies' boards of directors, is expected to close by mid-August, subject to approval by their shareholders and regulators.

The merger does not include several other entities bearing the Koll name, including Koll Construction; Koll Real Estate Group, a development and investment company; or Koll International, a resorts and recreational development company.
Koll Real Estate Services had 1996 revenues of $115 million and has about 2,400 employees in 278 offices throughout the United States and Asia.

CB also reported net income of $2.3 million, or 9 cents per share, for the first quarter ended March 31, vs. a loss of 5 cents per share in the year-ago period. Revenues rose 19 percent to a record $134.1 million from $112.7 million. CB has more than 4,000 employees.
CB's stock rose 37.5 cents to $23.375 early on Nasdaq.
